answer.evidence: The whole 16x64 sprite is a face-on masonry wall of stacked stone blocks with dark outline joints, which is a vertical face. The column scan shows light block faces (L~180-197) split by thin dark joint lines at rows 7, 13, 24-27 and 33. The pale 1-row lines at rows 14-15 and 25 are block highlights between joints. None is followed by eave shadow, and no band above them reads as a horizontal surface. The silhouette is 16 wide on every row, with no ellipse, roof or slope, and no visible contents. The base from row 48 dithers into dark water and green moss. This is a front elevation with no readable top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow grey stone column with a dark green base. It has no roof, door or windows, so it does not read as a whole building like the two references (tiled roofs, timber and plaster walls, doors). Its measured density is fine: 15 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, with 0% near-flat coverage. The stones are shaded one by one, but only about 4 grey steps are visible, against roughly 5-6 per material in the references. 85% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7% and 9% in the references, so the outline is a neutral near-black line rather than the dark tone of the adjacent material. That is the sticker look, and it counts against the piece. It fails on kind mismatch, neutral outline and shallower shading ramps.
